long_biography.plain_text:
Yizhaq Hajaj trained in law and business administration before earning a master’s degree in law. He and his brother Eido began developing property under the Hagag Group name in 2003, concentrating on purchasing groups and high-end residential and office projects. Their business secured control of a listed Israeli developer and assembled a prominent Tel Aviv portfolio.

Hajaj took the model abroad through Hagag Development Europe, making Bucharest its first major market. The European arm combines restored historic buildings, housing and offices, while the Israeli group continues urban-renewal and large mixed-use projects. As co-founder and controlling shareholder, Hajaj focuses on acquisitions and development strategy; professional executives now handle the listed company’s daily management.

uncertainties.detail: The exact English passport spelling in an exchange filing is Yizhaq Hajaj, while English-language company and industry sources use Yitzhak Hagag or Isaac Hagag and Hebrew sources use יצחק חג'ג'. The dossier retains the passport and source-record form and introduces the best-known public variant for continuity.

Reviewed first-party pages variously describe Hajaj as chairman, director, board controller, co-founder and controlling shareholder. The dossier uses the durable co-founder and controlling-shareholder relationship for the Israeli group and reserves chairman for Hagag Development Europe, while avoiding an unsupported current chief-executive title.

The brothers began real-estate activities under the Hagag Group name in 2003 and gained control of the listed company at the end of 2010. The dossier distinguishes the founder-built operating history from the later public-company platform.

Reliable sources establish that Hajaj and his brother founded and built the development platform, but do not document their starting family wealth or early financing in enough detail for a narrower self-made subtype.

The exact-person exchange filing establishes 9 December 1969 and Israel is already recorded as the birth country. No reliable source located supplies a city of birth, middle names or a second nationality, so those fields remain unproposed.

Reviewed sources differ on the precise year of the Romanian platform's establishment or market entry. The biographies therefore describe the Bucharest expansion without assigning a contested start year.

No identity-verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok, Wikipedia page or personal website met the verification threshold. The official Hagag Group website is proposed; the Forbes Romania interview is not a dedicated Forbes profile.

The existing biography centres on a private asset and its holding structure. That material was used only to identify the source record and is excluded from the replacement biographies, wealth classifications and tags.
